standard_prerequisites.name: For an ideal in a Noetherian ring the comparison between the derived tensor product with its powers and the ordinary products is a pro-isomorphism, which immediately gives a power factoring through the derived tensor product of the ideal itself
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies a short proof of the statement, after which the author gives an independent direct argument.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient by the ideal sits in a distinguished triangle with the ideal, so factoring through the derived tensor product with the ideal is equivalent to the vanishing of the composite into the derived tensor product with the quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Reformulates the goal as the vanishing of one morphism in the derived category.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite module annihilated by an ideal can be absorbed by a sufficiently high power of that ideal in the Ext group, so an obstruction element can be killed after increasing the power
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the successive factorization steps to be completed in finitely many rounds, which gives the required power.

core_obligations: Record that the statement follows from the pro-isomorphism between the powers of the ideal and the derived tensor products, and announce that a direct argument will also be given (proof lines 29744-29745).

Use the distinguished triangle relating the derived tensor product with the ideal, the module and the derived tensor product with the quotient to reduce the goal to the vanishing of the composite from a power of the ideal to the derived tensor product with the quotient (proof lines 29746-29752).

Choose generators of the ideal and factor the quotient map through the Koszul complex on those generators, reducing further to the vanishing of the composite from a power of the ideal into the tensor product of the module with the Koszul complex (proof lines 29752-29758).

Run the finite induction: suppose a power of the ideal factors through the truncation above degree t of that tensor product; the obstruction to factoring through the next truncation is an element of the Ext group of the power with the degree t homology, which is annihilated by the ideal, so after increasing the power the obstruction vanishes (proof lines 29758-29765).

Repeat this finitely many times, using that the Koszul complex is bounded, to reach the zero truncation and conclude that some power of the ideal factors through the derived tensor product of the ideal with the module (proof lines 29765-29767).
proof_roadmap: Reduce through the distinguished triangle to a vanishing statement for the composite into the quotient (proof lines 29744-29752).
Factor the quotient map through the Koszul complex and reduce to the tensor product with it (proof lines 29752-29758).
Kill the obstruction elements successively in the Ext groups to reach the zero truncation in finitely many steps (proof lines 29758-29767).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for an ideal in a Noetherian ring and a finite module there is a positive power of the ideal whose map to the module factors through the derived tensor product of the ideal with the module (statement lines 29736-29742). Besides the short proof through the known pro-isomorphism, the author gives a direct argument that reduces the goal through a distinguished triangle to the vanishing of a composite into the derived tensor product with the quotient, factors the quotient map through the Koszul complex, and then runs a finite induction in which the obstruction to improving the factorization is an element of an Ext group of a power of the ideal with a module annihilated by the ideal, which can be killed by raising the power (proof lines 29744-29767). The two reductions and the boundedness of the Koszul complex are what turn the statement into finitely many vanishing conditions. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
